page.layout: One page of text, with two round medallion portraits at the top, each with its inscription around the edge. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. A decorative woodcut ornament at the foot, without text.

main_text.p: ARTAXERXES Xerxis filius, cognomèto Longima-nus, quòd manum dextram finistra longiore haberet, Artaba-num cum filiis occidit, de patris nece vindictam sumens. impe-rauit Persis anno mundi 3497. ante Christum natum 465. hic à Metasthene Darius, ab Esdra Darius & Artaxerxes vocatur indifferenter. nam Persæ his duobus nominibus promiscuè utuntur, sicut & nos imperatores nostros Cæsares & Augustos, sine discrimine vocamus. Astu Artabanū, juvenis ad huc, gladio transfodit: nam finxit se arma velle commutare, si inermem aggressus egregio in juvene commento, inimicum ense traiecit. Just.li.3.&10.Hero.lib.7.Plutar.in Artaxerxe. imperauit annos 40. Vide item Esdr.1.lib.ca.4.&7.

ESDRAS Propheta fuit temporibus Artaxerxis, quē adiit, ab eóque petiit ut liceret Judæis reverti Jerusalem: & obtinuit. missus est igitur Esdras Jerosolymam, cum reliquiis vasorum Domini à Nabuchodonosore in Babyloniam abduc-torum, ac-ceptis ab Artaxerxe privilegiis ut liceret ei constituere judices ac præsides in populo Judæ, ac Jerusalē, collapsámque Judæo-rum remp. instaurare. Consulito 1. lib. Esdræ, 7. cap. hinc incipiunt septem Danielis hebdomades.

page.notes: The two medallion inscriptions are set around the coins; the left-hand one is partly worn, and the name ARTHAXERXES is uncertain. The woodcut ornament at the foot carries no text. A short stroke by the right-hand medallion is a scan mark, not print. The right-hand medallion legend ends "ET SACER" and is read from the image; the outer letters are partly faint. Printed abbreviations and the reference-style lines have been kept as printed. The two paragraphs are the printer's own; the first continues from no earlier page.
